Build the Atlantis calibration objective function

make_objfn.Rd

Creates the calibration objective function with calibration_objFn, wrapping run_model and the likelihood computation into a single callable used by calibrate.

Usage

make_objfn(setup, observed, aggregate = FALSE, forcing, ...)

Arguments

setup

Calibration setup object produced by calibration_setup, defining which targets belong to which phase.

observed

Named list of observed data used to evaluate the likelihood at each iteration, produced by calibration_data.

aggregate

Logical. If FALSE (default), the objective function returns per-target log-likelihood contributions as a named vector, enabling phased calibration where different parameter groups are optimised separately. If TRUE, returns a single aggregated scalar value.

forcing

Data frame of parameter metadata with at minimum columns paropt, parmin, parmax, and parphase. Row names are used as parameter names.

...

Arguments passed to run_model at every run: prefix, fg.file, biom.indx, run.prm and dt.timeseries. The shell script and the biology and harvest parameter files are found by run_model itself.

Value

The objective function. It takes par, a numeric vector of parameters in the transformed (log) scale, and returns a named numeric vector of per-target log-likelihood contributions.

Details

Setting aggregate = FALSE means the objective function returns per-target log-likelihood contributions as a named vector rather than a single scalar. This enables phased calibration, where different parameter groups are optimised in separate phases against their respective targets.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
  objfn <- make_objfn(setup, observed, forcing,
                      prefix = "outputFolder/outputSETAS",
                      fg.file = "SETasGroupsDem.csv",
                      biom.indx = "outputFolder/outputSETASBiomIndx.txt",
                      run.prm = "VMPA_setas_run_fishing_F_Trunk.prm",
                      dt.timeseries = 5)
  # Evaluate the objective function at the initial parameter values
  objfn(par = forcing[["paropt"]])
} # }
